vignette: Sudhir, a 33-year-old male of Southeastern Asian descent, works as a physical therapist at a local hospital. Married and dedicated to his profession, Sudhir's life took an abrupt turn when he was involved in a severe car accident about six months ago on his way home from work. The collision with a semi-truck left him hospitalized for several weeks and scarred both physically and emotionally. Sudhir vividly remembers the moment of impact; the sound of metal scraping against metal, the intense pain as the airbag deployed, and the subsequent confusion as he lay motionless in the wreckage. Since then, his mind has become a battleground where this traumatic event replays itself over and over again. Night after night, Sudhir awakens drenched in sweat, heart pounding with fear as if he were reliving that fateful evening. In the early mornings when he's trying to focus on work, intrusive memories of the accident often flood his mind unbidden. His hands shake slightly while examining a patient's X-rays, and occasionally, the sound of a siren outside sends a wave of panic through him, forcing him to pause and take several deep breaths before continuing with his tasks. Sudhir tries not to let these symptoms affect his work; he is deeply committed to helping others recover from their own traumas. His colleagues admire his professionalism and dedication, but they have noticed that Sudhir seems more distant and often cancels social gatherings or work meetings last minute. In reality, the thought of being in a car again fills him with dread, so much so that he now avoids driving altogether. His marriage has also been strained by his PTSD symptoms. His wife finds it difficult to understand why he withdraws into himself at times when they are out together. They used to enjoy weekend drives exploring new places, but since the accident, Sudhir avoids such activities entirely. He feels guilty for not being more present in their relationship and wonders if she would have married him had she known about these fears. Despite his efforts to keep a stoic front at work, Sudhir sometimes experiences intense anger towards the driver of the semi-truck that caused the accident. These bouts of rage often manifest as irritability with patients who seem less compliant or understanding during their therapy sessions. He recognizes this behavior and feels ashamed afterwards, further isolating himself from his colleagues. Sudhir's sleep is severely disrupted; he tosses and turns most nights, haunted by images of twisted metal and the sound of shattering glass. To cope, he often stays up late watching television to drown out these intrusive thoughts or meditates in an attempt to quiet his racing mind. However, even when he does manage to fall asleep, it's never restful; nightmares about being trapped in a vehicle are frequent, leaving him exhausted the next day. He has noticed that small things can trigger intense anxiety. The screeching of tires on wet pavement or hearing a car backfire can send shivers down his spine and cause an overwhelming urge to flee whatever situation he is in. These reactions have made it difficult for Sudhir to return to driving, which used to be something he enjoyed. Sudhir's PTSD symptoms significantly impact his ability to function both professionally and personally. His wife worries about him but struggles with how to support him when she feels pushed away. Despite these challenges, Sudhir remains committed to his role as a physical therapist, finding solace in helping others navigate their own recovery journeys. However, the persistent anxiety, flashbacks, and avoidance behaviors continue to affect every aspect of his life. Living day by day, Sudhir hopes that someday he can reclaim control over his fears and find peace with his past experiences.
